# VectoPrime

VectoPrime is a high-fidelity image-to-vector (SVG) conversion web application built by AHM Labs. It runs entirely client-side in the browser using a Rust-compiled WebAssembly port of the VTracer engine.

## Core Capabilities

- **Color Separation Masking**: Segments colored images into individual binary layers using a nearest-neighbor classification approach. This yields sharp edges and resolves wobbly lines/blurry borders.
- **Ramer-Douglas-Peucker (RDP) Simplification**: Reduces coordinate bloat by decimation of collinear vertices.
- **Tangent Bézier Curve Fitting**: Detects sharp corners based on turn-angle thresholds, fitting smooth cubic Bézier segments to curves while maintaining rigid points.
- **Geometric Primitive Detection**: Searches path coordinates for circular, elliptical, or rectangular geometry, replacing jagged path outlines with native `<circle>`, `<ellipse>`, and `<rect>` elements.
- **Gradient Creation**: Allows users to merge multiple traced flat colors into smooth SVG `<linearGradient>` structures directly in the browser.

## Built-In Features
- In-browser computation (completely serverless, zero data sent to external servers).
- Real-time settings sliders (precision, speckle filtering, corner thresholds, RDP epsilon, Bézier smoothing).
- Interactive SVG Editor (point tooltip details, click-to-delete paths/shapes, color palette isolation).
